main_text.head: INSTITUTIONUM METAPHYSICARUM, Tractatus Tertius, QVI EST DE Fructu consequente.
main_text.p: 1. CUm omnis ars omnisque disciplina, ad defectus naturæ humanæ auferendos institu-ta sit, ea sanè, quæ universalis erit disciplina, omnibus defectibus suo modo prospicere tenetur. Quare Metaphysica, quæ generalis fundamenti officio perfungitur, prout generalis est scientia, ubique suam utilitatem edere debet. Me-taphysici igitur est, illam usus universali-tatem primò ostendere, ac deinde quomodo, ex eâ petenda sit, docere.

2. Utilitas autem Metaphysicæ se extendit 1. ad Ϡεωρίαν & cognitionem τῶ ὄντων quâ ab intellectu ignorantia cum connexis ipsi vitiis auffertur. 2. Ad πρᾶξιν & operationem τῶν δεόντων, quâ voluntas, altera mentis potentia, quantum pote, perficitur.
1 Ϡεωρίαν: Greek, "theoria"; τῶ ὄντων: Greek, "tōn ontōn" as printed.

page.notes: The Greek words in paragraph 2 are reproduced as best read from the scan; the first Greek word of item 1 and the Greek terms are uncertain and may be misprinted. The large initial C of "CUm" is a woodcut-style initial joined to its word. Faint marks at the right edge and a stamp at the lower right are not transcribed.
